name: Stwo CUDA
headline: Prove Starknet faster on one H200.
summary: Research targets the CUDA proving stages for Starknet PIEs, wraps, and folds. Direct H200 proof and command timings are shown separately. The implemented h200-v1 judge scores full-command time; proof-only ranking is still an activation decision.

contract.timeScope: Judge wall time from adapted input to published proof; independent verification follows outside the timed interval.
contract.memoryScope: Independently sampled whole-device peak bytes during the measured command.

tracks.name: Latency
tracks.objective: Fastest adapted-input-to-publication time across the PIE, recursion, and pipeline basket.
tracks.why: Measures the full work needed to publish a proof from an adapted input.

tracks.name: Memory
tracks.objective: Smallest whole-device peak memory, subject to latency guards.
tracks.why: Dense PIEs must fit on one H200; whole-device peak captures transient allocations too.

tracks.name: Balanced
tracks.objective: Best normalized whole-command time × whole-device peak memory trade-off.
tracks.why: Explores the Pareto trade-off. A capacity proxy, not a cost claim.

families.name: Cairo proofs
families.description: Standalone Cairo proofs of single- and multi-block Starknet PIEs, chosen to stress different builtins. The scored command starts with an adapted PIE and ends with a published proof.

families.name: Fold proofs
families.description: Canonical multiverifier folds over distinct, already wrapped and verified circuit leaves. The fold command is timed through proof publication.

families.name: Cairo → wrap → fold
families.description: Adapted PIEs all the way to one recursive root: every Cairo proof, every wrap and every fold, in one case.

cases.title: Range-check 96 + mod
cases.description: One-block range-check-96 and modular arithmetic outlier.

cases.title: Four-block mix
cases.description: Four contiguous blocks with a high step count.

cases.title: Near capacity
cases.description: One-block, EC-heavy, close to the device memory ceiling.

cases.title: Two-leaf fold
cases.description: One fold proof over two distinct, already wrapped circuit leaves.

cases.title: Eight-leaf tree
cases.description: Seven fold proofs over eight state-continuous ten-block mainnet leaves.

cases.title: Serial, two leaves
cases.description: Two Cairo proofs, two wraps and one fold to the root, as separate processes.

cases.title: Batched, two leaves
cases.description: The same two Cairo proofs, wraps and fold in one resident CUDA process, so setup is reused.

tiers.name: Intake
tiers.description: Patch paths, file types, size and base commit are checked without running candidate code. Under a minute.

tiers.name: Smoke
tiers.description: A trusted worker rebuilds from source, runs focused tests, then one PIE and one recursion case with independent verification.

tiers.name: Qualify
tiers.description: The public basket plus a private holdout, once each, with exact security and output gates.

tiers.name: Rank
tiers.description: Fresh A/A calibration and at least three paired ABBA rounds of adapted-input-to-publication time and whole-device peak memory. Every track uses the same measurements; the receipt is signed.

participate.title: Check data and set up
participate.body: Pull public inputs and verify hashes, then run setup. It creates the ignored editable prover checkout at ./workspace/stwo-zig/ (singular workspace), which is absent from a fresh clone and from GitHub.
participate.command: git lfs pull && python3 challenge.py check-data && python3 challenge.py setup

participate.title: Edit the CUDA paths
participate.body: Run python3 challenge.py paths to find the generated checkout. Edit only the five CUDA directories in benchmark.json; spec/CODE_MAP.md names exact entry files for Cairo, wrap, fold, runtime, and publication. CPU, Metal, and Rust are read-only references.

participate.title: Capture the patch
participate.body: Writes candidate/changes.patch and refreshes the derived CUDA manifests. Update candidate/NOTES.md with the mechanism, focused checks and measurements.

participate.title: Build and smoke
participate.body: Builds both arms and the pinned verifiers, then runs one Cairo case and one fold case on the H200.
participate.command: python3 challenge.py setup --build && python3 challenge.py benchmark --tier smoke --track balanced

participate.title: Qualify and rank
participate.body: Run the whole basket once, then paired ABBA rounds that score every eligible track.

participate.title: Package and submit
participate.body: Commit candidate/changes.patch and candidate/NOTES.md in your fork and open a PR against the challenge repository. NOTES.md explains the CUDA change; the patch is the reviewable source diff. Once intake is live, also submit the fork's HTTPS URL and full commit SHA to POST /submissions.
participate.command: git add candidate/ && git commit -m "candidate: <mechanism>" && git push

rules: Correctness gates every track: each Cairo proof must pass the pinned Rust verifier and every root must match its reference.
Do not change proof security, public outputs, verifier code, fixture selection, timers, measurement, or the contract.
Any failed required case removes the submission from every track.
No CPU proving fallback, skipped proof stages, or proving work shifted outside the measured command.
A new leader must beat the current one by at least 1% and clear the paired A/A noise band.
The score counts adapted-input-to-publication time and whole-device peak memory; phase timers are diagnostics.

stages.name: Cairo proof
stages.summary: Proves an adapted Starknet PIE with the Stwo Cairo AIR, on the GPU.

stages.name: Wrap
stages.summary: Proves, inside a circuit, that a Cairo proof verifies. The result is a uniform circuit leaf that recursion can consume.

stages.name: Fold
stages.summary: One canonical multiverifier proof that verifies two child proofs. Folds repeat until a single root remains.
